title: Fix Loop Mode Line Selection Bug - Goes to Wrong Line
description: Loop mode has a consistent bug where it goes to the PREVIOUS line instead of the correct one. This happens in TWO scenarios: (1) When clicking a line to loop, it briefly highlights the line BEFORE the clicked line, then moves to correct line. (2) When the loop restarts, instead of staying on the current line, it jumps to the line BEFORE it. This is a timing/index calculation bug.

relevantCode: handleTimeUpdate - calculates active line based on current video time
handleLineClick - handles clicking a line to play/loop it
isLoopSeekingRef - (existing) attempt to prevent flash during loop seek
activeLineIndex state - the currently highlighted line
Loop mode logic that seeks video back to line start

bugAnalysis.symptom1: Click line N → line N-1 flashes → then line N highlights
bugAnalysis.symptom2: Loop restarts → goes to line N-1 instead of staying on line N
bugAnalysis.likelyCause: Time calculation uses wrong boundary (end time vs start time) or off-by-one in line index lookup
bugAnalysis.singleModeClue: Single mode: plays line, then advances to NEXT line and stops - this suggests the time-to-line mapping has boundary issues

acceptanceCriteria.text: Read src/routes/song.$songId.tsx focusing on handleTimeUpdate and loop logic
Identify the time-to-line-index calculation - find the off-by-one or boundary bug
Check if line boundaries use startTime <= time < endTime or startTime < time <= endTime
Fix the line index calculation to correctly identify current line at any given time
When clicking line N in Loop mode: line N highlights IMMEDIATELY (no flash to N-1)
When loop restarts: line N stays highlighted (no flash to N-1)
Watch 5+ loop cycles - same line stays highlighted the ENTIRE time
Single mode: click line N, plays line N, then advances to N+1 and pauses (expected)
Fluid mode: lines advance correctly with video (no wrong-line issues)
Test with line 1 (first line) - no crash or weird behavior at boundary
Test with last line - no crash or weird behavior at boundary

debuggingApproach: 1. Add console.log in handleTimeUpdate: log currentTime, calculated lineIndex, and line boundaries
2. Click a line and observe: what time does it seek to? What lineIndex is calculated?
3. At loop restart: what time triggers the re-seek? What lineIndex does it calculate?
4. The bug is likely: when time === line.endTime, it's matching line N+1 instead of line N
5. Fix: adjust boundary check to be inclusive on start, exclusive on end (or vice versa)
